problems.title: Least integer above a radical sum
problems.question: Find the least integer greater than √12+√27.
problems.idea: Combine like radicals.
steps: Its value is approximately 8.660, between 8 and 9.
problems.note: The Georgian suffix after the radical sum means “than”; it is not a subtraction of 9. The only available source is printed Variant N4; the earlier sorting called it Variant 1 because it was the first available file. A printed Variant I is not present. These solutions explicitly follow the available N4 paper.

problems.title: Angle sum in a pentagon with parallel sides
problems.question: In pentagon ABCDE, BC∥AE and ∠D=50°. Find ∠C+∠E.
problems.idea: The two angles along transversal AB sum to 180°.

problems.title: What an isosceles triangle cannot do
problems.question: Which statement is impossible for an isosceles triangle: obtuse, all acute, two angles sum to 90°, or all three angles different?
problems.idea: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles.
formulas: Equal sides imply equal opposite angles.
steps: The first three cases occur, for example with angles (40°,40°,100°),(60°,60°,60°),(45°,45°,90°).
Three different angles contradict the equal base angles.

problems.title: Tangent from coordinate increments
problems.question: A=(4,1),B=(5,5),C=(8,1). Find tan∠BAC.
problems.idea: AC is horizontal, and AB rises 4 while moving right 1.
steps: The angle is acute and its tangent is 4/1=4.

problems.title: Largest numbers with given digit counts
problems.question: How much less is the greatest three-digit number than the greatest five-digit number?
problems.idea: Write the two numbers explicitly.

problems.title: Follow the parentheses
problems.question: Evaluate ((500+1000÷4)÷5+200)·4-1600.
problems.idea: Work from the innermost operations outward.

problems.title: Travelled distance as a fraction of the whole
problems.question: After travelling 24 km, a traveller has one fifth of the route left. Find the whole route.
problems.idea: The travelled part is four fifths.

problems.title: Use the ordering to bound a sum
problems.question: 6,a,5,b,2,c,1 are in decreasing order, with a=b+c. Which listed value 2.8,3.2,3.8,4.8 cannot be b?
problems.idea: We have a≥5 and c≤2.
steps: The other values can work, for example (b,c,a)=(3.2,1.9,5.1),(3.8,1.5,5.3),(4.8,1.1,5.9).

problems.title: Two right triangles form a quadrilateral
problems.question: Right triangles ABC and BCD share BC, with right angles at C and B. ∠BAC=45°,AC=3,BD=5, and A,D lie on opposite sides of BC. Find area ABDC.
problems.idea: Add the two triangle areas.
steps: Their interiors lie on opposite sides of BC, so the sum is 12.

problems.title: An incenter angle equation
problems.question: O is a triangle’s incenter and ∠BOC=3∠BAC. Find ∠BAC.
problems.idea: Use the standard incenter angle formula.

problems.title: Root squares from Vieta’s formulas
problems.question: Find the sum of squared roots of x²-7x+2=0.
problems.idea: Use the root sum and product.

problems.title: A rectangle inside an equilateral triangle
problems.question: M∈AB,K∈BC,T∈AC of equilateral ABC; MNKT is a rectangle and ∠AMT=80°. Find ∠KTC.
problems.idea: Find angle ATM in triangle AMT, then use TK⊥TM.
steps: Since TA and TC are opposite rays, ∠MTC=140°.
The rectangle gives ∠MTK=90°, with TK inside ∠MTC.

problems.title: Cancel factored polynomials
problems.question: Evaluate [(a-2)/(a+3)]·[(a²-9)/(a²-5a+6)] at a=2016.
problems.idea: Factor both quadratics.
steps: Every numerator factor cancels, leaving 1 when a≠-3,2,3.
The supplied a=2016 satisfies those restrictions.

problems.title: Midpoints halve a general quadrilateral area
problems.question: In quadrilateral ABCD of area S, K and L are midpoints of CD and AB. Find area AKCL.
problems.idea: Remove triangles AKD and BLC from the full quadrilateral.
formulas: Area AKD=(1/2)area ACD; area BLC=(1/2)area ABC.
steps: The removed areas total half of area ABC+ACD, which is S/2.
The remaining quadrilateral AKCL therefore has area S/2.

problems.title: Read one point after reducing by the period
problems.question: The shown function has period 6. Find f(26).
problems.idea: Subtract four periods.
steps: The plotted point at x=2 has height 1.

problems.title: Parallel section through a trapezoid’s diagonal crossing
problems.question: A trapezoid has bases 2 and 3. Find the parallel segment through the diagonal intersection between the legs.
problems.idea: That length is the harmonic mean of the bases.
steps: Similarity places the crossing at the same fractional height on both diagonals. Linear interpolation of the parallel widths gives 2ab/(a+b).

problems.title: A rational graph is unbounded above
problems.question: Find the greatest value of y=1/(x²-4x+1).
problems.idea: Inspect its denominator near a zero from the positive side.
steps: It can be positive and arbitrarily close to zero, making the reciprocal arbitrarily large.

problems.title: A zero coefficient with a nonzero constant
problems.question: When does ax=bx+b-1 have no solution?
problems.idea: Bring the x terms together.
steps: There is no solution exactly when a-b=0 but b-1≠0.
If both vanish every x works; if a-b≠0 there is one solution.

problems.title: A tangential isosceles trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has inradius 3 and diagonal 10. Find its larger base.
problems.idea: The height is twice the inradius.
steps: Thus ((B+b)/2)²=100-36=64, so the base half-sum and leg are both 8.
The larger base is half-sum plus half-difference.

problems.title: Reflection across the x-axis
problems.question: Reflect y=3x+5 across the x-axis.
problems.idea: Keep x and negate the output.

problems.title: Perpendicular chords tangent to a concentric circle
problems.question: Two perpendicular chords of the larger circle are tangent to the smaller concentric circle. Their intersection divides a chord into parts 4 and 10. Find the smaller radius.
problems.idea: The chord midpoint is halfway between its endpoints.
formulas: Distance from the intersection to the chord midpoint=(10-4)/2.
steps: Because the other chord is perpendicular and tangent to the inner circle, that midpoint-to-intersection distance equals the inner radius.

problems.title: More than one identity survives domain checks
problems.question: Which listed equalities are identities: x²/x=x; a√b=√(a²b); -a√a=√(a³); -a²√(-a)=-√(-a⁵)?
problems.idea: An identity must hold at every input in its natural domain.
steps: x²/x=x is an identity for x≠0.
a√b=√(a²b)=|a|√b fails for negative a and positive b.
-a√a=√(a³) fails for positive a, because the two sides have opposite signs.
For a≤0, √(-a⁵)=√(a⁴(-a))=a²√(-a), so the final equality is also an identity.
problems.answer: Choices a and d are both identities on their natural domains.
problems.note: If an unstated restriction a≥0 were intended for the second equality, choice b would also hold. The source does not specify such a restriction.

problems.title: Worker-hours scale with the number of walls
problems.question: Four workers build one wall in 8 hours. How long do six equally productive workers need for three walls?
problems.idea: Count worker-hours.
steps: Six workers complete 96 worker-hours in 96/6=16 hours.

problems.idea: Count both possible assignments to the two axes.

problems.title: Bisector versus altitude
problems.question: In triangle ABC, A=60°,B=80°. Find the acute angle between the A-bisector and the altitude from C.
problems.idea: The bisector makes 30° with AB.
formulas: The altitude is perpendicular to AB.
steps: The acute angle between a line at 30° to AB and one at 90° to AB is 90°-30°=60°.

problems.title: Compare two area formulas
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base 10 cm and altitude to an equal side 8 cm. Find the equal side length.
problems.idea: Express its area using either base.
formulas: If equal side=l and base altitude=h, then 5h=4l and l²=h²+25.
steps: Taking the positive root gives l=25/3.

problems.title: A tangent circle through another side midpoint
problems.question: ABC is right at C, AC=4,BC=3. A circle is tangent to AB at its midpoint and passes through the midpoint of BC. Find its radius.
problems.idea: Its centre lies on the normal to AB at the tangency point.
steps: A normal to AB is (3,4), so let the centre be P=M+t(3,4). Its squared radius PM² is 25t².
Because N is on the circle, PN²=(2+3t)²+(4t)²=25t².
problems.note: The scan says the circle crosses BC at its midpoint; this is not a second tangency condition.

problems.title: A prime-power factorization
problems.question: Find natural n,k and prime p satisfying n²+28n+52=p^k.
problems.idea: Factor the left side into two positive integers differing by 24.
steps: Both factors exceed 1, so n+2=p^u,n+26=p^v with 1≤u<v, and p^u(p^(v-u)-1)=24. Thus p is 2 or 3.
For p=2, the second factor is odd and divides 24. It must be 3, giving v-u=2 and 2^u=8. Thus u=3,v=5,n=6,k=8.
For p=3, 3^u divides 24, so u=1. Then 3^(v-1)-1=8, giving v=3,n=1,k=4.
Direct checks: n=6 gives 256=2⁸; n=1 gives 81=3⁴.
